title: Beyond Earth: Settler - Reality vs Game Transparency
principle: NASA source URLs provide scientific context; a linked URL alone does not verify every adjacent game parameter.

entries.real_world: Lunar sidereal rotation is about 27.3 Earth days; lunar solar day is about 29.5 Earth days.
entries.game_model: Any fixed 14-day night is a simplified mid-latitude/equatorial scenario; south-pole lighting is location-dependent.

entries.real_world: NASA provides broad lunar surface day/night temperature ranges; polar crater and rim conditions differ by site.
entries.game_model: Destination temperature fields are illustrative global extremes, not verified Shackleton rim local forecasts.

entries.real_world: Oxygen consumption varies with person and workload.
entries.game_model: Constant 0.84 kg/person/day is a fixed simulation baseline from consumption.json; source needs independent numerical review.

entries.real_world: NASA develops life-support, power, and ISRU systems; no NASA reference here verifies all eight game module power ratings.
entries.game_model: Module kW, costs, capacities, wear and construction times are game-balancing parameters.

entries.real_world: Water recovery efficiency depends on the system and configuration.
entries.game_model: The recipe uses 8 water units from 10 wastewater units for balancing, not as a claim of ISS performance.

entries.real_world: NASA reported MOXIE produced 122 g oxygen total over 16 runs and up to 12 g/hour at best.
entries.game_model: Mars CO2-to-oxygen recipe uses abstract resource units and accelerated processing.

entries.real_world: Crew atmosphere and radiation limits are subject to mission-specific standards and exposure durations.
entries.game_model: Thresholds in alarms.json are game alerts and must not be described as universal NASA fatality thresholds.

entries.real_world: NASA discusses space weather, EVA planning, life support and crop systems.
entries.game_model: Wheel weights, choices, effects and rewards are fictional teaching mechanics.

entries.real_world: NASA educational sources support science topics.
entries.game_model: 12 board tiles, rewards, difficulties and time limits are game design, not NASA mission procedures.

entries.real_world: NASA describes candidate landing regions and ongoing lunar exploration planning.
entries.game_model: Shackleton rim is a fictional playable base placement, not an established NASA operating base.

classification_definitions.NASA_VERIFIED_CONTEXT_GAME_BALANCE_ASSUM: Scientific context checked against cited NASA page; game mechanic invented.
classification_definitions.NASA_CONTEXT_PLUS_GAME_SIMPLIFICATION: General NASA science context used with a location/time simplification.
classification_definitions.SOURCE_ATTACHED_NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFI: Citation present but exact numerical support not independently confirmed.
classification_definitions.GAME_BALANCE_ASSUMPTION: Numbers and mechanics invented for gameplay, not NASA values.
classification_definitions.REQUIRES_SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW: Do not advertise threshold as NASA-validated.
classification_definitions.GAME_SETTING_ASSUMPTION: Narrative setting based on real locations, not an actual established facility.

implementation_notes: Do not count a source URL as proof of all game fields.
Use the original six JSON files unchanged; review assumptions before final judging.
